rules.problem: Diagnosis concept is generic Herpes simplex rather than oral herpes; 'painful' dropped.

Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from mouth symptoms
rules.problem: 'check for anaphylaxis' -> possible; BP <90/60 encoded as SBP<90 OR DBP<60, matching the gold file. Exposure timing dropped.

rules.rule: Urgent: mouth symptoms with inability to open mouth or anaphylaxis signs
rules.problem: Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention ... Refer urgently'; and/or structure faithful.
Page says 'If no better or uncertain of cause: Check Hb. If < 12g/dL (woman) or < 13g/dL (man), anaemia likely' — an 'X likely' with no probable-anaemia diagnosis rule.

summary: Most consequential: the aphthous ulcer rule fires on any 'Ulcer of mouth', dropping the page's 'painful ... with central white patch', so other mouth ulcers become probable aphthous ulcer. The page's 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12 woman / < 13 man, in the cracked-corners column) has no diagnosis rule. Smaller issues: the allergen exposures lose the 'past few hours' window, contact-dermatitis itching has no finding site, and the herpes diagnosis uses the generic Herpes simplex instead of Oral herpes simplex infection.
